name: Crack Chicken Chili

ingredients.buy: 2 1/2 cups, drained and rinsed (about two 15 oz cans)
4 cups, drained and rinsed (just under two 15 oz cans)
optional: 2/3 cup sour cream, plus avocado or extra cheese, to serve (140 g)

writer_notes: Cream cheese is placed in the pot at step 1 (start), reading the source's 'all ingredients except cheese' as excluding only the shredded Mexican blend; this is the only way the bought 14 oz cream cheese line is used, so do not move it to the melt step or it orphans.
Sour cream is written as a to-serve topping only (step 4), matching its 'optional, to serve' buy line; it is not cooked into the batch.
Cost is carried as the ${{cost_ps}} token because no literal cost_ps appears in the locked view. Protein is the {{protein}} token; calories are stated as the bound 'under 600' (542 per locked view).

DATA FLAG: cayenne buys at 3.5 tsp total for 14 servings and exceeds chili powder (1 3/4 tsp); faithful to source's 2 tsp scaled up but genuinely hot, so prose stays heat-neutral rather than overselling spice.
DATA FLAG: bean cup yields are inconsistent for the same can count - kidney 2 1/2 cups from 'about two 15 oz cans' vs black beans 4 cups from 'just under two 15 oz cans'.
DATA FLAG: source lists plain 8 oz cream cheese; locked line is 14 oz of 1/3 Fat Cream Cheese, a fat-level swap and scale-up that the macros assume.

prose.intro_html:
Crack chicken chili earns the name honestly. It is the creamy, ranch-spiked, bacon-loaded cousin of regular chili, and once a container of it is waiting in your fridge you stop thinking about takeout. Here is the part that matters for the crew: it clears {{protein}} grams of protein a serving and still lands under 600 calories a bowl. That is comfort food without the comfort food regret.

Better still, it is a dump and go slow cooker meal. You load the crock in the morning, walk away, and come home to fourteen dinners done. No searing, no browning, no standing over a pot. That is my kind of Tuesday.
prose.shop_smart:
This is a pantry and cans build, which is exactly why it stays cheap. Start with the chicken. You need 3 1/2 pounds of boneless skinless breast, and that is almost always a better deal in a big family pack than in little trays. Buy the largest pack that fits your freezer and you are set.

The cans do the heavy lifting here. Grab two 14.5 ounce cans of corn, two 15 ounce cans of diced tomatoes, two 15 ounce cans of kidney beans, two 15 ounce cans of black beans, and two 4 ounce cans of green chiles. Fire roasted tomatoes are worth grabbing if the shelf has them, but plain diced will not hurt a thing.

Cream cheese comes in 8 ounce bricks and you need 14 ounces, so two bricks covers it with a little left over for a bagel. Ranch seasoning runs about one and three quarter packets, so a two packet box has you covered. Bacon is 18 slices cooked crisp, which a standard pack gets you. And buy the Mexican blend shredded by the bag, not the pricey little cup.
prose.make_it:
This one is built for the slow cooker, so there is very little to it. Into the crock go the chicken breasts, the bone broth, the ranch seasoning, the garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne, paprika and chili powder, then the drained corn, the tomatoes, the kidney beans, the black beans, the green chiles, the chopped crisp bacon and the cream cheese. Everything except the shredded Mexican blend cheese goes in now. Give it a stir, put the lid on, and cook on high for 4 to 5 hours or low for 6 to 8.

When you have about 30 minutes left, lift the chicken breasts out, shred them with two forks, and drop the meat back into the pot to finish. The cream cheese will have melted into the broth by now and made everything creamy.

Right at the end, stir in the shredded Mexican blend cheese and let it melt through. Taste it, and go easy the first spoonful because there is real cayenne in here. Then it is ready to portion.
prose.portion_html:
Fourteen containers is the target, and the honest way to split it even is the scale, not your eyeballs. Set your empty container on a kitchen scale and zero it out. Weigh the full pot, subtract the pot, then divide that number by 14. That is your gram weight per container. Scoop to that number every time and every crew member gets the same dinner, same macros, no one shorted.

Hold the sour cream, avocado and extra cheese until serving. Those go on top the day you eat it, not into the storage container, so nothing goes watery in the fridge.
prose.cost_closing_html: Run the numbers and this whole pot breaks down to ${{cost_ps}} a serving. That is a creamy, protein packed, bacon studded dinner for less than the drink you would order with takeout, and you made fourteen of them in one afternoon of doing basically nothing.
prose.upsell_html: Every recipe on Thrifty Crew runs through the same cost engine, so you know what a meal costs before you ever turn on the crock. Membership is a dollar a month, right about the price of one serving of this chili. Join the crew and eat like this every week.

head.description: Crack chicken chili built for meal prep: a creamy, bacon-loaded slow cooker chili with over 47 grams of protein a serving and fourteen budget dinners from one pot.
head.keywords: crack chicken chili, chicken chili meal prep, slow cooker chili, high protein chili, crockpot crack chicken, budget meal prep dinner
steps: Add the chicken breast, bone broth, ranch seasoning, garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne, paprika, chili powder, drained corn, diced tomatoes, kidney beans, black beans, green chiles, chopped bacon and cream cheese to the slow cooker. Stir, cover and cook on high for 4 to 5 hours or on low for 6 to 8 hours.
With about 30 minutes left, lift out the chicken, shred it with two forks and return it to the pot to finish cooking.
Stir in the shredded Mexican blend cheese until it melts through.
Weigh the full pot, divide by 14 and portion evenly across the containers. Top with sour cream, avocado or extra cheese to serve.
